subject.title: fix(line): AI-assisted - requireMention can now optionally gate non-text messages with bounded pending-media retention

question: Should OpenClaw support `requireMentionForNonText`, `pendingMediaLimit`, and the documented process-local best-effort retention semantics for LINE groups?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent, but it creates a new stateful user-facing configuration and scheduling contract that automated review cannot approve as product direction.

options.title: Accept the opt-in contract
options.body: Keep the backward-compatible defaults and documented lifecycle, then require real LINE proof before merge.

options.title: Gate without retention
options.body: Remove the pending-media queue and explicitly treat skipped non-text media as lossy if a simpler contract is preferred.

options.title: Defer non-text gating
options.body: Leave current non-text passthrough behavior unchanged until a different channel UX is selected.

recommendation.title: Accept the opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Keep the backward-compatible defaults and documented lifecycle, then require real LINE proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The plugin-boundary refactor makes this the strongest current ownership signal for LINE runtime and configuration direction.
